correctness.rationale: Every order-five binary de Bruijn rotation class corresponds bijectively to a 32-cycle among the successor permutations induced by sixteen local bijective incoming-to-outgoing edge matchings. A six-letter Abelian square at an entering edge ax and outgoing edge xb is equivalent to a+sum(x[0:2])=sum(x[2:4])+b. Thus an explicit local integer score sums over all 16 vertices. The standalone verifier tests all 65,536 matchings and finds exactly 2,048 one-cycle cases; it independently generates 2,048 circuits by edge-disjoint DFS, recomputes all cyclic factors, and verifies the exact distribution and group orbits. The search space is mathematically exhaustive rather than sampled. The 2,048 total matches the known binary de Bruijn count 2^(2^4-5). Finite limits and conventions are explicit.

originality.rationale: A complete full-text comparison against arXiv:1701.00948 locates its assertions about Abelian-square-rich infinite words (not distribution of Abelian-square counts across de Bruijn rotation classes). Existing generic counts of Abelian squares and de Bruijn successor construction do not imply the new weighted 32-cycle census. Actual searchable published results about binary order-five de Bruijn cycles concerned maximum discrepancy, longest palindrome, or linear complexity, which do not logically determine this local equal-Parikh statistic. No equivalent histogram or symmetry classification was found in the searches; unindexed specialized results remain a real risk. Abstract-only relevant sources are flagged rather than asserted full-text NOT_COVERING.

value.rationale: All length-five factors of an order-five binary de Bruijn cycle occur exactly once, but first extensions to length six are not fixed. Counting equal-Parikh adjacent triples is a canonical Abelian-repetition statistic exactly at this first unconstrained factor length. The theorem completely classifies its attainable values, sharp extrema, multiplicities and complement-reversal symmetry orbits across all 2,048 cycles, and reduces the statistic to a structural 16-switch Euler-tour score. This nonconstant nine-value distribution and orbit refinement answer a precise natural finite question; the contribution is not merely a checker, a textbook deduction from the de Bruijn count, or a random subset sample.
